thread:
maria: Heads up — noticed a p99 latency regression for acme-prod starting at ~2024-10-02T17:12Z right after runtime v2.18. Deploy shows big increase in kv/prefix cache misses. Dashboard: https://metrics.redwood/acme/prod/latency p50 stable, p95 up ~120ms, p99 jumped 400ms -> ~1.8s.

maria: Quick snapshot — cache miss rate for prefix cache went from 6% -> 38% in the timeframe. Eviction_count spiked on a few nodes. Suspect key entropy change from the new prefix-normalization flag.

sara: Support ticket #S-12345 opened by ACME earlier. They reported user-facing slowdowns and a few timed-out streams. Customer impact: intermittent UI stalls for ~5% of requests. They asked if this is a config rollbackable on our side. :frowning:

devon: Can we get a heap of the KV cache state and a sample of prefix keys around the spike? If it's normalization flapping, we might see duplicate logical keys with different physical keys. Run:

```
# on node with high eviction_count
REDWOOD_DEBUG=1 ./tools/kv-inspect --node pg-12 --show-prefixes --sample 200 > /tmp/kv-sample.txt
jq -r '.prefixes[] | {prefix, cardinality, recent_evictions}' /tmp/kv-sample.txt | sort -r -n -k2 | head -n 30
```

maria: pasted the kv-inspect output into Gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/kv-sample-5480001111 (contains noisy keys but you can see many near-duplicates: e.g. `org:acme:chat:session:abc123`, `org:acme:chat:session:abc123.0`, `org:acme:chat:session:abc123-` )

kevin: I ran the inspect on the affected shard. Observed ~3x logical duplicates for several hot prefixes; normalization introduced trailing separator toggles for empty metadata fields. Evictions happening because effective cardinality ballooned. Repro steps I used:

```
# repro harness (local)
python tools/repro_prefix_entropy.py --pattern 'org:acme:chat:session:{id}{suffix}' --suffixes "['', '.', '-']" --qps 300 --duration 300
# watch cache metrics
curl localhost:9000/metrics | grep prefix_cache_miss_rate
```

kevin: Immediate mitigation — I flipped the runtime flag `prefix-normalization=v1` -> `prefix-normalization=legacy` on the 4 nodes with highest eviction_count. That reduced miss rate from 38% -> 9% within 2m and p99 fell back to ~420ms. I also applied a short-lived prefix-tagging rollout so the normalization path is isolated to canary.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated for runtime:v2.18 on shard pg-12 by kevin at 2024-10-02T17:34Z.

devon: Nice fast rollback. Can we add a short-term circuit: cap per-prefix tracked cardinality at 10k keys and emit a high-cardinality alert? If we cap too low we might break customers with legitimate high-cardinality patterns, but better to fail closed than OOM/latency spike.

maria: Agreed. Immediate action items:
- kevin: follow up with a PR to add per-prefix cap + metric (high_cardinality_truncation_count) — target: 48h.
- devon: add an alert for prefix_cardinality > threshold (per-tenant) and eviction_rate > X for 2m.
- sara: notify ACME that we've mitigated, rolled back normalization, and are tracking a fix.

sara: Sent update to ACME: "We identified a prefix normalization regression that increased effective key cardinality and caused cache thrash. We've rolled back the new normalization flag for your shard and are observing p99 recovery. We're implementing a per-prefix cap and follow-up fix." They replied :relieved:.

kevin: Long term fixes I want in the backlog: canonicalize prefix tokens (strip trailing separators), add deterministic normalization tests in e2e, and implement adaptive eviction that considers per-prefix hotness instead of global LRU. I'll open tickets and link to this thread.

maria: Thanks all. Closing immediate incident (no pager escalation). Please paste PR/issue links here when available so support can keep ACME updated. :thumbsup:
